user.title: ADS-B station
user.description: What runs on your receiver? Anything that serves an aircraft.json works: dump1090, dump1090-fa and SkyAware, readsb and tar1090. Add the Flightradar24 feeder on top only if you actually run fr24feed.

fr24feed.title: Flightradar24 feeder
fr24feed.description: Enter the address of your Flightradar24 feeder. Home Assistant reads the status page that fr24feed serves on your own receiver.

data_description.host: The IP address or hostname of the device running fr24feed, for example 192.168.5.7.
data_description.port: The port of the fr24feed status page. The default is 8754.

piaware.title: FlightAware feeder
piaware.description: Enter the address of the machine running PiAware. The port is the one its status page is served on, 8080 by default.

data_description.host: The IP address or hostname of the device running PiAware, for example 192.168.5.7.
data_description.port: The port serving status.json. FlightAware's own tooling uses 8080; a station whose web server was taken over by something else may serve it elsewhere.

planefinder.title: Plane Finder feeder
planefinder.description: Enter the address of the machine running pfclient. The port is the one its web interface is served on, 30053 by default.

data_description.host: The IP address or hostname of the device running pfclient, for example 192.168.5.7.
data_description.port: The port of the pfclient web interface. The default is 30053.

receiver.title: ADS-B receiver
receiver.description: Enter the address of the machine running your decoder. Home Assistant looks for its aircraft.json in the usual places.

data_description.host: The IP address or hostname of the device running the decoder, for example 192.168.5.7.

aircraft.title: ADS-B receiver
aircraft.description: Home Assistant can also read the aircraft.json of your decoder for the number of aircraft received, the message rate and the maximum range. Leave the field empty to skip this. Leave it empty if another entry on this station already reads the decoder, or its aircraft will be counted twice.

data_description.aircraft_url: The full URL to aircraft.json, for example http://192.168.5.7:8080/dump1090/data/aircraft.json. Detected automatically when possible.

receiver_url.title: aircraft.json
receiver_url.description: This is where the data comes from, so it is required. Any decoder that serves an aircraft.json works, whichever network you feed.

data_description.aircraft_url: The full URL to aircraft.json, for example http://192.168.5.7/tar1090/data/aircraft.json. Detected automatically when possible.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the feeder
error.invalid_response: This address does not serve an fr24feed status page
error.cannot_connect_aircraft: Failed to connect to the ADS-B receiver
error.invalid_aircraft_response: This URL does not serve an aircraft.json
error.aircraft_url_required: Without a feeder, an aircraft.json URL is required

abort.wrong_feeder: This address belongs to a different feeder

data_description.scan_interval: How often the station is read, in seconds. Everything runs on your own network, so a short interval is fine.
data_description.proximity_radius: How close an aircraft has to be to count as nearby, in kilometres. Ten is roughly what you can see and hear.
data_description.proximity_max_altitude: How high an aircraft may be and still count as nearby, in feet. Leave it empty and the radius alone decides, which is worth knowing about: a radius is a circle on the ground, so without a ceiling an airliner at 36,000 feet is overhead. It applies to what is nearby, what is overhead and what counts as a passage, and to nothing else: the aircraft still counts as received, still sets range records, and an emergency squawk is still reported at any height.
data_description.map_aircraft: Puts every aircraft inside the nearby radius on the map as its own entity, for as long as it is there. Nothing is registered and nothing is kept, so they leave no trace once they have flown on; that also means they cannot be renamed or hidden individually, and they are not listed under this station's device.
data_description.look_up_routes: No aircraft broadcasts where it is flying from or to, so this is the one figure that has to be asked of a service on the internet. It uses routeset, the same source tar1090 does. Only the aircraft inside the nearby radius are looked up, and answers are kept for the day.
data_description.watchlist: Aircraft worth knowing about whenever they turn up, one to a line. There is no radius: this asks whether the aircraft is in the air at all, however far away. A line can be a hex code (484123), a registration or a callsign (PH-BXA, KLM123), an aircraft type (EC35) or a squawk (7700).

error.unreadable_watchlist: These lines are not a hex code, a registration or callsign, an aircraft type or a squawk: {lines}

look_up_aircraft.name: Look up aircraft
look_up_aircraft.description: Answers with everything this station knows about one aircraft, by hex code or callsign, out of its last poll.

aircraft.name: Aircraft
aircraft.description: The hex code or the callsign, in either case. An aircraft this station is not hearing answers with nothing, which is not an error.

config_entry.name: Station
config_entry.description: Which station to ask. Only needed when more than one of your entries carries a receiver.

list_aircraft.name: List aircraft
list_aircraft.description: Answers with every aircraft this station is hearing that matches, nearest first. Without a single filter that is everything the decoder is holding, which reaches far beyond the nearby radius.

max_distance.name: Within
max_distance.description: How far out to look, in kilometres. Aircraft that never sent a position are left out, because there is no telling how far away they are.

min_altitude.name: Higher than
min_altitude.description: In feet. Aircraft that report no altitude are left out.

max_altitude.name: Lower than
max_altitude.description: In feet. Aircraft that report no altitude are left out.

military.name: Military
military.description: On for military traffic only, off for everything but.

category.name: Category
category.description: The emitter category an aircraft broadcasts, A0 to D7. A7 is a helicopter and B6 a drone.

config_entry.name: Station
config_entry.description: Which station to ask. Only needed when more than one of your entries carries a receiver.

install_sentences.name: Install voice sentences
install_sentences.description: Copies the spoken sentences this integration ships into your configuration directory, where Assist reads them from. Run conversation.reload afterwards, or restart.

speak.name: Speak an answer
speak.description: Returns one of the five spoken answers as text, ready for a sentence trigger to say back. Needs no sentence files.

question.name: Question
question.description: Which of the five to answer: what is overhead, how many are up there, which is closest, whether a kind of traffic is in range, or where the aircraft overhead is going.

kind.name: Kind
kind.description: For the traffic question only: military, helicopter or drone.

language.name: Language
language.description: Which language to answer in. Defaults to the language of your Home Assistant; English and Dutch are spoken, anything else is answered in English.

config_entry.name: Station
config_entry.description: Which station to ask. Only needed when more than one of your entries carries a receiver.

no_receiver.message: No ADS-B station has read its receiver yet, so there is nothing to answer with.

several_receivers.message: More than one station carries a receiver ({stations}), so this call has to say which one to ask.

station_not_loaded.message: That station is not set up, so it cannot be asked anything.

station_without_aircraft.message: {station} has no receiver of its own, so it hears no aircraft. Ask the entry that carries your decoder.

sentences_not_written.message: The sentences could not be written to your configuration directory: {error}
